proposals: QatarEnergy should publish fuel-gas consumption per tonne of LNG for its trains fitted with starter-helper motors, before and after installation, so that the feed gas freed by helper motors at Ras Laffan is stated as a measured outcome rather than inferred from the physics, as this piece had to do.

Equinor should publish annual results from the Hammerfest LNG electrification, including CO₂ actually avoided against the 850,000-tonne target and drive availability after grid disturbances, so that the grid ride-through risk flagged by its own engineers can be tracked in operation.

The US Energy Information Administration should publish plant-level fuel-gas and electricity consumption for each LNG export terminal, including all-electric Freeport LNG, so that turbine-driven, helper-assisted and electric-drive trains can be compared on their actual own-use energy per tonne.
